candidates.source_name: NBS PSD2 register – machine-readable JSON API (subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2)
candidates.why_relevant: Daily-updated JSON list of Slovak PSD2 third-party providers (AISP/PISP/PIISP) with business name, address, ICO and per-service start/end dates. New entries are the earliest machine-detectable signal that a new payment actor exists — which precedes the compliance/MLRO/CTO hiring wave this cell tracks. Also the canonical actor-list seed for snowballing into companies not covered by startup media.
candidates.access_status: open, no auth reported; JSON endpoint
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled daily GET of the JSON endpoint; diff against previous snapshot on ICO + service start dates to emit 'new TPP' and 'ceased TPP' events. A signed variant is reported at /api/psd2signed for integrity checking.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for the PSD2 register, then followed to the NBS register landing page which documents the API

brief: For Slovak fintech, neobank and crypto/payments scale-ups, hiring and leadership intelligence has no editorial home and must be assembled from three tiers. The register tier is unusually strong and cheap: NBS publishes the PSD2 TPP list as a daily-updated JSON API at subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2, runs a post-MiCA crypto supervision section (only six licensed SK CASPs remain), and the Obchodný register — surfaced with change alerting by FinStat — captures statutory-body changes that are frequently the sole public trace of a C-level hire at a seed-stage firm. The signal tier is job boards (Profesia dominates; a live example is an MiCA-regulated SK fintech advertising a lead compliance officer) plus company team-page diffs, backed by sk-language trade and startup media — FinReport, Forbes.sk, Startitup/Fontech — for funding rounds that precede the hiring wave. The main risks are that the richest channels (founder LinkedIn posts, FinStat alerts, Crunchbase/Tracxn) are all walled or paid, that seed actor names are already stale (TrustPay now trades as finby, with a reported Malta licence), and that key role titles circulate in English inside Slovak text, so keyword sets must be bilingual within a single query.
